front_layout.split_note: SPLIT 2026-08-27, and every part names where its number comes from. Until today this 1950 was ONE undivided remainder, because the page prints the SUM and refuses to divide it - and that was the right recording while nothing had asked. The kitchen asked: the door was not drawn, and a column with no door on a LayOut elevation reads as an open shelf. WHAT IS PRINTED on printed p.162: the family height 2340, the jumbo drawer front (39 handle, 36 gola), the contents list, and the words 'custom-sized door' - which is the catalog saying, in its own vocabulary, that this door's height is not an article dimension. WHAT IS ESTABLISHED: 600 for an oven H.60 opening, recovered from front stacks five times over (claude/findings-2026-08-25-tall-h210-appliance-columns.md 1) and corroborated on THIS page by the position above it - C92657 prints 96/39/39, and 960+390+390 leaves exactly 600. WHAT IS DERIVED, and it is ours: 1950 - 600 - 600 = 750 for the door. WHAT THE RENDER SHOWS, read at 600 dpi 2026-08-27: door, opening, opening, drawer, and the two openings measure within a few per cent of each other - which excludes a 450 microwave opening, the only competing reading, since that would have left a 900 door. Andriy reached the same 750 independently by the same subtraction. SCOPE (learned rule 4): this is one position on one page. The twins C63640 at H.222 and C42640 at H.210 carry the same undivided shape and have NOT been split - nothing has asked them yet.
front_layout.opening_note: BOTH OPENINGS ARE 600 AND THE PAGE DOES NOT SAY WHICH MACHINE TAKES WHICH. The title is 'oven and microwave oven'; the drawing shows two equal openings with a divider between them and labels neither. So both carry the geometry class oven_h60 - a 600 opening - and which of the two the oven goes in is a per-order fact, not a catalog one. Naming the upper one 'microwave' would have been an invention with a 50 per cent chance of being backwards, and nothing geometric turns on it: they are the same size.
